title: Customer Intake Cohort Priority Hub and Commitment SLOs
creator: Leah Morales
description: Problem: We receive high-touch requests from strategic accounts at varying cadence and quality. Current top-account intake is ad-hoc, leading to inconsistent commitment times and missed expectations. Goal: Build a lightweight 'Cohort Priority Hub' that converts signals (account ARR, incident exposure, exec escalation, ROI runway, legal/compliance constraints) into a ranked intake queue, an SLO for commitment latency by cohort, and a negotiation UI hook for comms. This hub will feed roadmap lanes and trigger the correct engagement path (self-serve, concierge, sales-assisted). Outcome: predictable commitment windows (e.g., 2, 6, 12 weeks) per cohort, transparent rationale for prioritization, and audit trails for enterprise negotiations.
acceptance_criteria: Cohort model implemented with at least 3 input signals and documented weights
Priority queue visible in Console PM dashboard with sortable fields
Commitment SLOs defined and enforced: Gold=2w, Silver=6w, Bronze=12w
Communication templates for each path saved in docs and linked to tickets
Pilot completed with 5 strategic accounts and feedback collected
milestones: M1: Signal taxonomy & weight matrix approved (2026-03-01)
M2: Intake API + scoring lambda implemented (2026-03-21)
M3: PM Dashboard prototype with ranked queue (2026-04-01)
M5: Rollout to VIP intake lane (2026-04-20)
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal intake for Sales/Customer Success for 2 weeks
Phase 1: Pilot with 5 paid strategic accounts (data collection + qualitative interviews)
Phase 2: Expand to top 30 accounts and connect to roadmap cadence
Phase 3: Publicize SLOs internally and add to executive update
notes: Design wants a compact justification card per ticket (see design brief link)
We need legal to confirm we can publish cohort names referencing deal size
Consider adding automated Slack notifications to assigned PMs when high-risk signals spike
decisions: Use a weighted linear scorer instead of black-box model for auditability
Commitment SLOs will be calendar-week based rather than sprint-based
Pilot will not change GTM promises; it informs acceptance windows only
tradeoffs: Simplicity vs fidelity: starting with 3 signals reduces accuracy but increases explainability
Hard SLOs increase predictability but risk overpromising if engineering capacity is constrained
risks: Over-indexing on ARR could deprioritize product-wide quality issues
Ambiguous cohort labels may frustrate CSMs if not well communicated
open_questions: What exact weight should Exec Escalation carry vs. Incident Severity?
Should we expose cohort assignment to customers in their dashboard?
